page: OVHcloud r3-1024-flex is a memory-optimized cloud server hosted on a KVM hypervisor. The instance features 128 dedicated AMD EPYC physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, configured with a single thread per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 1024 GB, establishing an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is limited to a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, and network throughput is provisioned with a 20 Gbps baseline interface. No GPU accelerators are present on this server type.

Benchmark testing demonstrates high compute and memory bandwidth capabilities under parallel loads. In stress-ng evaluations, multi-core CPU performance reached 288,912.83, placing it within the top 10% of tested instances. Cached read memory bandwidth measured 10,848.37 GB/sec, while uncached large-block read transfers sustained 271.22 GB/sec. In database caching benchmarks, the configuration achieved 163.82 million Redis SET operations per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered 1,140.05 GB/sec, reflecting efficient multi-core data processing capabilities.

The primary hardware tradeoff is the compact 50 GB local NVMe disk, which necessitates external or network-attached storage architectures for persistent datasets larger than system memory. Additionally, the CPU flags indicate standard AVX support without AVX-512 extensions. OVHcloud r3-1024-flex is suited for massive in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large-scale extract-transform-load (ETL) routines, and parallelized data analytics tasks.
description: The OVHcloud r3-1024-flex is a memory-optimized cloud instance providing 128 dedicated AMD EPYC physical cores clocked at 2.3 GHz and 1024 GB of system RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Built on a KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, the configuration pairs high memory density with a 20 Gbps network connection and a 50 GB local NVMe SSD, omitting GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations highlight high parallel throughput, ranking in the top tier for multi-core compute and achieving 163.82 million Redis SET operations per second alongside cached memory bandwidth exceeding 10,800 GB/sec. The modest local storage footprint represents a primary operational tradeoff, requiring external storage volumes for substantial persistence requirements. The instance is suited for large-scale in-memory key-value stores, distributed analytics, high-throughput caching, and memory-intensive batch processing.
